stem: During the final time-out immediately before incision, the circulating nurse notes that the operative schedule lists a right-knee procedure while the consent and marked site indicate the left knee. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Allow the incision because the marked site is visible and the discrepancy can be corrected in the record afterward
options.B: Stop the procedure and require the team to resolve and verify the patient, procedure, and site discrepancy before incision
options.C: Ask the scrub person to choose which document is most reliable so the surgeon can proceed without delay
options.D: Proceed with the site on the schedule because the operating-room schedule takes precedence over the consent and site marking

rationale: The Universal Protocol is designed to prevent wrong-person, wrong-site, and wrong-procedure events. The final time-out occurs immediately before incision with active participation by the immediate procedure team. A discrepancy among the schedule, consent, and marked site must be resolved before the procedure begins; documentation cannot be corrected after an incision to make an unresolved mismatch safe. The nurse should stop progression and participate in verification rather than selecting one conflicting source unilaterally.
educational_objective: If patient, procedure, or site information conflicts during the final surgical time-out, the nurse stops progression and ensures the discrepancy is resolved and verified before incision.
source_locator: Standards FAQ: Universal Protocol — Pre-procedure Verification; final time-out immediately prior to incision; involvement of all immediate procedure-team members; principles preventing wrong-person/wrong-site/wrong-procedure surgery
source_claim_supported: The Joint Commission states that the final time-out must occur immediately before incision with the immediate procedure team and that the Universal Protocol uses standardized verification to prevent wrong-person, wrong-site, and wrong-procedure surgery.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p. 24 (PDF page 27): protect client from injury; properly identify client; verify appropriateness and accuracy of a treatment order
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — correct patient/procedure/site verification
correction_summary: Replaced perioperative-role trivia with a high-consequence wrong-site prevention scenario using the current Joint Commission Universal Protocol. Removed role-description distractors and focused on the circulating nurse's safety responsibility during the final time-out.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current Joint Commission FAQ last updated 2026-01-09 and 2025 National Performance Goal page verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Timing, team participation and prevention purpose of the final time-out are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Unsafe; unresolved discrepancy cannot be deferred to documentation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; stop and resolve before incision.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; one team member should not arbitrarily select among conflicting records.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; no single conflicting schedule entry can override unresolved verification discrepancies.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B satisfies the verification process before incision.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address management of the discrepancy; no role-trivia cue remains.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked whether site marking alone could resolve the conflict, whether surgeon confirmation alone suffices, and whether emergency exceptions apply; stem is elective final time-out with unresolved conflict, so B remains uniquely best.
